Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Let's now plot the graph of [MATH: y=\tan x,] with [MATH: x] in radians.

Content:
First, let's create a table for some of the values that we know:

Content:
| [MATH: x] | [MATH: -\dfrac\pi 2] | [MATH: -\dfrac\pi 3] | [MATH: -\dfrac\pi 4] | [MATH: -\dfrac{\pi} 6] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: \dfrac{\pi} 6] | [MATH: \dfrac{\pi} 4] | [MATH: \dfrac{\pi} 3] | [MATH: \dfrac\pi 2] |
| [MATH: \tan x] | [MATH: \text{undefined}] | [MATH: -\sqrt{3}] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: \sqrt 3] | [MATH: \text{undefined}] |

Content:
Now, let's plot these points to estimate the graph of [MATH: y=\tan x.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e70a041387968f2f2f7c0d821e983aef]

Content:
If we inspect the unit circle carefully, we see that the function [MATH: y=\tan x] repeats itself every [MATH: \pi] radians. Therefore, we can extend our plot using this periodicity property:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/807f126c657c1494d51946a57b2e9629]

Content:
Some key characteristics of the graph of [MATH: y=\tan x] are as follows:

Content:
- The domain of the function is almost [MATH: x\in (-\infty ,\infty)] except for the points where the function is undefined, namely [MATH: x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots]
- The range of the function is [MATH: y\in (-\infty, \infty).]
- The period of the function is [MATH: \pi.]
- There is no minimum or maximum value.
- The zeros occur at [MATH: x=0,\pm\pi,\pm2\pi,\dots]
- The graph has vertical asymptotes at the points not in the domain: [MATH: x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots.] At each asymptote, the graph tends to [MATH: \infty] from the left and [MATH: -\infty] from the right.

---

Item 8 — Tutorial: Graphing the Cotangent Function

Content:
The cotangent is the reciprocal of the tangent:
[MATH: \cot x = \dfrac{1}{\tan x}.]

Content:
To plot the graph of [MATH: y=\cot x,] with [MATH: x] in radians, we create a table with some known values:

Content:
| [MATH: x] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: \dfrac{\pi}{6}] | [MATH: \dfrac{\pi} 4] | [MATH: \dfrac{\pi} 3] | [MATH: \dfrac\pi 2] | [MATH: \dfrac{2\pi} 3] | [MATH: \dfrac{3\pi} 4] | [MATH: \dfrac{5\pi}{6}] | [MATH: \pi] |
| [MATH: \tan x] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: \sqrt{3}] | [MATH: \text{undef.}] | [MATH: -\sqrt{3}] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}] | [MATH: 0] |
| [MATH: \cot x] | [MATH: \text{undef.}] | [MATH: \sqrt{3}] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: -\sqrt{3}] | [MATH: \text{undef.}] |

Content:
Plotting these points gives the following graph:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4cb7a46d805709cbb4c2469276b62cc5]

Content:
Notice that:

Content:
- a zero on the graph of [MATH: y=\tan x] corresponds to a vertical asymptote on the graph of [MATH: y=\cot x,] and
- a vertical asymptote on the graph of [MATH: y=\tan x] corresponds to a zero on the graph of [MATH: y=\cot x.]

Content:
The cotangent inherits its periodicity from the tangent, so the period of the cotangent is [MATH: \pi.] Using this periodicity property, we can extend our plot of the cotangent function:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/367e5f6f7c2017657d36cc1bbc306915]

Content:
Some key characteristics of the function [MATH: y=\cot x] are:

Content:
- The domain is all real numbers except at the integer multiples of [MATH: \pi,] namely [MATH: x= 0,\pm\pi,\pm 2\pi,\dots]
- The range of the function is [MATH: y\in (-\infty, \infty).]
- The period of the function is [MATH: \pi.]
- There is no minimum or maximum value.
- The zeros occur at [MATH: x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots]
- The graph has vertical asymptotes at the points that are not in the domain: [MATH: x=0, \pm\pi,\pm 2\pi,\dots,] and at each asymptote, the graph tends to [MATH: -\infty] from the left and [MATH: \infty] from the right.
